Available skills:
- allium: Give your AI agents something more useful than a prompt. Velocity through clarity.
- distill: Extract an Allium specification from an existing codebase. Use when the user has existing code and wants to distil behaviour into a spec, reverse engineer a specification from implementation, generate a spec from code, turn implementation into a behavioural specification, or document what a codebase does in Allium terms.
- elicit: Run a structured discovery session to build an Allium specification through conversation. Use when the user wants to create a new spec from scratch, elicit or gather requirements, capture domain behaviour, specify a feature or system, define what a system should do, or is describing functionality and needs help shaping it into a specification.
- ponytail: >
- ponytail-audit: >
- ponytail-debt: >
- ponytail-gain: >
- ponytail-help: >
- ponytail-review: >
- propagate: Generate tests from Allium specifications. Use when the user wants to propagate tests, generate test files from a spec, write tests for a specification, create property-based tests, produce state machine tests, check test coverage against spec obligations, or understand what tests a specification requires.
- tend: Tend the Allium garden. Use when the user wants to write, edit, update, add to, improve, clarify, refine, restructure, fix or migrate Allium specs. Covers adding entities, rules, triggers, surfaces and contracts, fixing syntax or validation errors, renaming or refactoring within specs, migrating specs to a new language version, and translating requirements into well-formed specifications. Pushes back on vague requirements.
- test-code-review: Review code for bugs, security issues and style problems. Use when asked to review a pull request, audit a function or find problems in source code.
- test-python-plotting: Create charts and plots in Python with matplotlib or pandas, such as histograms, bar charts, line graphs and data visualisation from CSV files.
- test-sql-queries: Write and optimise SQL queries for PostgreSQL or MySQL, including joins, aggregation, indexes and slow query tuning.
- test-writing-edit: Edit and polish prose. Proofread essays, rewrite emails, improve tone, shorten paragraphs and fix grammar in documents.
- weed: Weed the Allium garden. Find where Allium specifications and implementation code have diverged, and help resolve the divergences. Use when the user wants to check spec-code alignment, compare specs against implementation, audit for spec drift or violations, sync specs with code or code with specs, or verify whether the implementation matches what the spec says.
- witness: Independently witness that an Allium loop's convergence claim is true and was reached honestly. Use when the user wants to verify a loop's self-report, confirm tests really pass and no generated test was weakened, produce a convergence certificate or witness record, gate CI on a trustworthy signal, or check that an autonomous run did not cheat its way to green.
- wriggle-add-scene: Add a new game screen to Wriggle (title, pause, settings or menu) by subclassing Scene and registering it with SceneManager, then switching to it. Use when creating a new screen or changing between scenes.
- wriggle-add-weapon: Add a new weapon, projectile, ammo type or explosion to Wriggle, following the grenade pattern in Weapons/Grenades.cs with ammo in the player inventory. Use when creating or changing weapons, ammo, throws, fuses or explosions.
- wriggle-assets: Add or load runtime assets for Wriggle, such as textures, maps, sprites and other files the game reads at runtime. Use when adding a PNG, map or any file the game loads.
- wriggle-build-and-test: Build the Wriggle game and run its xUnit tests with dotnet. Use for compile errors, running tests, checking which spec tests fail, or verifying that a change works.
- wriggle-debug-tools: Add ImGui debug widgets, scene debug controls, live tuning sliders and developer hotkeys to Wriggle. Use when adding debug UI, tuning values live, or adding a developer shortcut.
- wriggle-dependencies: Manage Wriggle's NuGet packages and version pins, including Raylib-cs 7.0.1 and rlImgui-cs 3.2.0, and the xUnit test packages. Use when adding a package, upgrading raylib or ImGui, or diagnosing a native crash after a dependency change.
- wriggle-overview: Overview of the Wriggle C# raylib worms-style game, its folder layout, scenes, weapons, physics and world code. Start here for any question about how the Wriggle project is organised.
- wriggle-physics-and-terrain: Change Wriggle's physics bodies, collisions, gravity, radial impulses and destructible terrain carving, including loading the terrain map. Use when working on movement, bouncing, explosions that carve holes, or terrain collision.
- wriggle-run-game: Run the Wriggle game window, edit gameconfig.json window settings, and take screenshots, including automated screenshots with GAME_SHOT_PATH. Use when launching the game, checking visuals, or capturing a screenshot.
- wriggle-spec-driven: Use the Allium behaviour specs in Wriggle's specs/ folder as the source of truth for game rules. Use when adding or changing a game rule, writing or checking a spec, or mapping code to spec obligations.
- wriggle-write-tests: Write xUnit tests for Wriggle in tests/Wriggle.Tests in the project's spec-obligation style. Use when adding a test, covering new non-trivial logic, or fixing a failing test.
Answer with exactly one skill name from this list, or 'none' if no skill fits.

- wriggle-write-tests: Write xUnit tests for Wriggle in tests/Wriggle.Tests in the project's spec-obligation style. Use when adding a test, covering new non-trivial logic, or fixing a failing test.
